agentic-commerce.rationale: Product truth, policy, authority, and transaction readiness must be challenged before agent-mediated buying is recommended.

ai-discovery-strategy.rationale: AI discovery claims depend on current answer-surface behavior and must stay evidence-bound.

autonomous-media-operations.rationale: Automated media requires explicit authority, monitoring, rollback, and human escalation boundaries.

behavioral-marketing.rationale: Behavioral interventions require a plausible mechanism rather than decorative psychology labels.

brand-strategy.rationale: Brand choices must reconcile memory effects, commercial outcomes, and short-versus-long horizon trade-offs.

campaign-strategy.rationale: Campaign direction must be distinctive to the diagnosed job instead of collapsing into generic creative advice.

category-strategy.rationale: Category decisions depend on category maturity, competitive frame, and the market structure actually observed.

commerce-feed-intelligence.rationale: Merchant and product feeds must be complete, current, consistent, and policy-safe before downstream automation relies on them.

commerce-media-strategy.rationale: Closed-loop commerce signals can overstate causality and require explicit bias and incrementality scrutiny.

competitive-intelligence.rationale: Competitive conclusions need substitute analysis and adversarial testing rather than competitor feature copying.

content-strategy.rationale: Content decisions need a specific audience job, role, and distribution logic rather than a generic editorial calendar.

conversational-advertising.rationale: Conversational ad flows must progress real intent without inventing context or overstating AI surface behavior.

conversion-strategy.rationale: Conversion changes must connect observed friction to a plausible behavioral mechanism and business outcome.

creator-commerce.rationale: Creator recommendations must separate discovery, media, affiliate, commerce, and incremental value.

customer-research.rationale: Customer research must preserve observed language and buying situations without fabricating psychology or prevalence.

go-to-market.rationale: GTM sequencing must follow a diagnosed market and route-to-market choice before channel execution.

incrementality-design.rationale: Counterfactual claims require an explicit incremental design rather than attribution-only evidence.

market-diagnosis.rationale: Market diagnosis must establish the commercial problem before tactics or channel prescriptions are allowed.

marketing-experimentation.rationale: Experiments need a falsifiable mechanism, decision rule, and interpretation boundary.

marketing-measurement.rationale: Measurement architecture must distinguish platform attribution, business outcomes, and causal evidence.

marketing-signal-strategy.rationale: Automation signals require quality, freshness, provenance, and value semantics before optimization.

media-strategy.rationale: Media allocation must reconcile reach, channel role, commercial constraints, and time horizon.

offer-strategy.rationale: Offer architecture must connect proof and proposition to margin, capacity, and commercial reality.

positioning-strategy.rationale: Positioning choices depend on category frame, alternatives, maturity, and credible differentiation.

pricing-strategy.rationale: Pricing architecture must connect willingness to pay, economics, discount rules, and commercial constraints.

product-marketing.rationale: Product story and launch messaging must connect demonstrable product truth to customer language and buying criteria.

retention-strategy.rationale: Retention choices must distinguish lifecycle causes from acquisition quality and respect unit economics.

segmentation-strategy.rationale: Segmentation must improve an actual decision and avoid substituting demographic labels for buying behavior.
